Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)
34-year-old male with 6-week history of persistent fatigue, generalized myalgias/arthralgias, and a self-resolving annular calf rash that appeared ~2 weeks after hiking in the U.S.  
Likely issues:  
• Suspected early disseminated Lyme disease—rash compatible with erythema migrans; timing and outdoor exposure support.  
• Alternative/overlapping considerations: post-viral fatigue (EBV/CMV), hypothyroidism, anemia or vitamin deficiencies.  
Plan:  
• Order blood tests: CBC, renal panel, liver panel, TSH, Lyme serology; consider iron studies, vitamin D, EBV/CMV serology if initial work-up negative.  
• Arrange telephone follow-up 1 week after bloods to review results.  
• If Lyme serology positive, commence appropriate antibiotic regimen (e.g., doxycycline—drug/dose to be determined).  
• Provide safety-net advice: seek care for new fevers, spreading rash, neurologic or cardiac symptoms.  
• Encourage graded return to exercise as tolerated; maintain adequate nutrition and hydration.  

Management Plan
-  Blood tests ordered as above; patient to book phlebotomy and schedule follow-up tele-consultation.  
-  Supportive care; no new medications initiated pending results.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. Lyme disease – High likelihood: compatible rash, outdoor exposure, timing, current fatigue/arthralgia.  
2. Post-viral fatigue (e.g., EBV/CMV) – Moderate likelihood: preceding sore throat/low-grade fever, persistent fatigue.  
3. Hypothyroidism – Moderate likelihood: fatigue and myalgias; to be screened via TSH.
